title: Trump wants future Iran talks focused on nuclear file, not Hormuz, sources say
body: This detail matters less for immediate price action and more for how traders should read the ceiling on any near term de-escalation in the Strait of Hormuz. If Washington genuinely prefers to keep its own bilateral leverage reserved for Tehran's nuclear program rather than engaging directly on Hormuz access, that suggests the shipping and tolls track will continue to run through Oman and the Gulf states largely without direct US involvement, for better or worse. That could mean slower progress on a durable reopening framework, since the party with the most military leverage over the strait is choosing not to anchor its diplomacy there, but it could also mean less risk of the US complicating an Oman brokered deal with separate nuclear related demands. Either way, this points to continued reliance on regional diplomacy rather than a US-Iran breakthrough as the more likely path to easing the current oil risk premium, reinforcing why postponements like the one already covered are consequential rather than incidental. --- Earlier: Weekend: Tanker hit by projectile in Hormuz as fresh attacks reported at sea Oil gap higher: Saudi pipeline shut after drone attack as Hormuz meeting is postponed --- Washington appears content to let Iran, Oman and the Gulf states handle Hormuz diplomacy on their own, while keeping its own leverage with Tehran reserved for the nuclear question.

title: Weekend: Tanker hit by projectile in Hormuz as fresh attacks reported at sea
body: Fresh attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz land at a sensitive moment for oil, coming right as regional diplomacy over the waterway has stalled and just after the Saudi East-West pipeline closure removed an alternative export route. Confirmed damage to a single tanker would not typically move crude on its own, but the combination of a verified UKMTO incident and an unverified Iranian claim of a second, more serious attack reinforces the broader narrative of an unresolved and escalating threat to tanker traffic through one of the world's most important chokepoints. With shipping volumes through Hormuz already well below pre-war norms, incidents like this tend to reinforce existing risk premia rather than introduce a new one, keeping upside pressure on crude intact until the security picture stabilises or a credible ceasefire or shipping arrangement actually holds. --- Earlier: Iran says Hormuz meeting with Gulf states postponed at request of regional countries Globex is open and oil has jumped higher while stocks have slumped. title: Tesla's flying Roadster demo to land after years of missed reveal dates
body: The Roadster reveal is unlikely to move Tesla's share price in any lasting way on its own, given the stock is currently priced by the market largely on robotics and software narratives rather than a low volume halo car. Saudi Arabia suspended operations on the East–West pipeline as a precaution after Thursday's attacks and has not yet indicated when flows will resume. At the same time, talks between Iran and several Gulf states on creating a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz were postponed, according to Oman's Foreign Minister, Badr Albusaidi. Reports indicated that Saudi Arabia had reservations about the plan, while Bahrain said it would not take part. The closure of the East–West pipeline has underscored its critical role in sustaining energy supplies across the Middle East, especially as the United States and Iran remain deadlocked over control and security of Hormuz. title: CICC warns $100 oil could bring demand destruction into view

title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7083 – Reuters estimate
body: The fixing mechanism matters most right now because of what it has been signalling over recent weeks. The PBOC set its reference rate at the widest weak side deviation from market estimates in six months in late August, after the yuan touched a three and a half year high, a clear sign of discomfort with the pace of gains rather than the level itself. Traders should read this as the central bank applying the brakes rather than attempting to reverse the broader trend, since the yuan has still risen a meaningful amount against the dollar this year. The balancing act Beijing faces is straightforward: a stronger currency helps with capital stability and import costs, but too rapid a rise risks eroding export competitiveness at a time when the domestic economy is showing renewed signs of softness. Watching the gap between the daily fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the more reliable ways to gauge PBOC intent in the days ahead.---The daily fixing is Beijing's quietest but clearest tool for telling markets how fast it wants the yuan to move, and lately the message has been to slow down. Summary: The PBOC sets the daily USD/CNY reference rate, or midpoint, at around 0115 GMT, one of the most closely watched signals in Asian FX markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, allowing the yuan to trade within a band of plus or minus 2% around the daily midpoint during onshore hours.

title: Musk highly confident SpaceX will launch Nvidia AI computers into orbit in 2027
body: Musk's comment reinforces a theme that has already moved both stocks once this year, when Nvidia rose more than 4% after SpaceX confirmed it would build exclusively on Nvidia hardware for its AI ambitions, while SpaceX shares initially fell over 10% before paring losses on investor uncertainty about execution risk and capital intensity. A reaffirmed 2027 launch timeline for the Starmind AI satellite keeps the Nvidia read through intact and gives some support to the idea that space based compute demand could become a durable, if still early stage, source of orders for Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform. For SpaceX specifically, the market's reaction is likely to hinge less on today's confidence signal and more on whether Starship's launch cadence and reliability can plausibly support the scale Musk is describing, given analyst modelling already extends capacity projections out to 2031 and the plan remains contingent on unresolved engineering questions around cooling, radiation hardening, and heat dissipation in orbit. --- Earlier: Tesla's flying Roadster demo to land after years of missed reveal dates ---- Musk is reaffirming an aggressive timeline to put Nvidia powered AI computers into orbit next year, a bet on space based compute that keeps both companies' fortunes increasingly intertwined.

title: Carney explores Canada as EU associate member, WSJ reports
body: This is a longer horizon structural story rather than an immediate market mover, but it speaks to the ongoing repricing of Canada's trade relationships since the tariff dispute with Washington escalated. A deeper EU tie-up, if it advances, would represent a meaningful diversification of Canadian trade exposure away from the United States across goods, services, energy, and critical minerals, which could support the loonie over time by reducing dependence on a single, currently strained trading relationship. That said, the practical hurdles are significant. The EU has historically been inflexible on membership style arrangements, and the difficulty in ratifying even the existing, more modest Canada-EU trade deal, still incomplete more than a decade on, suggests any associate membership framework would take years to negotiate and implement. Markets should treat this as a directional signal on Canada's strategic pivot rather than something with near term FX or rates implications. --- Carney is testing whether Canada could become an EU associate member, a strategic hedge against a deteriorating trade relationship with Washington that could reshape everything from worker mobility to energy infrastructure.

title: Jordan Inflation Rate at 3-Month Low
body: Jordan's annual inflation rate eased for the third consecutive month in August 2026, slowing to 2.66% from 2.70% in July. This was the lowest reading since May, reflecting the waning impact of earlier fuel price increases. The government raised fuel prices by 11% in April—its first hike since the onset of the Middle East conflict—and made a partial upward adjustment again in May. Transportation remained the largest driver of inflation, contributing 1.12 percentage points, as transport prices rose 7.02%, up from a 6.77% increase in July. Rents were the second-biggest contributor, adding 0.76 percentage points, with housing costs increasing 3.81%, slightly below July's 3.86%. Inflation in food and non-alcoholic beverages also moderated, contributing 0.23 percentage points compared with 0.70% previously. On a monthly basis, the consumer price index (CPI) fell 0.25% in August, following a 0.18% decline in July, marking a second consecutive month of deflation in headline prices. title: Heating Oil Hits Record High
body: US heating oil prices have surged to a record high of about $5.10 per gallon, as escalating supply disruptions intensify concerns in an already tight distillate market. The shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline has aggravated existing shipping challenges through key regional straits, heightening worries about crude availability and further constraining refinery feedstock supplies. At the same time, disruptions along Yemen's Red Sea coast are limiting traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, while Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries are tightening diesel supplies amid Russia's ongoing export restrictions. According to EIA data, US distillate inventories were 13% below the five-year average in the week ended September 4, even as refineries ran at 97.8% of capacity, leaving little room to increase production. With seasonal agricultural demand now picking up and the winter heating season approaching, consumption is likely to strengthen further, adding additional pressure to already strained distillate supplies. title: Gold Remains Under Pressure
body: Gold hovered near $4,300 an ounce on Monday after logging three consecutive weekly declines, pressured by surging oil prices and mounting expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy. Oil jumped to near four-month highs after Saudi Arabia shut a key pipeline used to bypass the Strait of Hormuz following drone attacks. The prolonged conflict in the Middle East has delivered an inflationary shock to the global economy, reinforcing expectations of a hawkish interest-rate stance. Futures markets now imply about an 86% probability that the Fed will raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday. Data released Friday showed US consumer inflation holding at 3.4% in August, unchanged from July and in line with forecasts, while the monthly CPI rose 0.4%, the fastest pace in three months. US producer prices also quickened in August as the war involving Iran drove wholesale energy costs higher, and labor-market indicators continued to signal resilient employment conditions. title: US Futures Drop on AI Safety Concerns
body: US stock futures declined on Monday amid mounting concerns over the safety of advanced artificial intelligence development, while investors shifted their focus to this week's Federal Reserve policy meeting. On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said AI companies should slow the development of their most sophisticated models due to safety risks, and he pledged to introduce additional safeguards at his firm. Separately, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the ChatGPT maker does not plan to go public this year. On the monetary policy front, markets are currently pricing in roughly an 86% chance of a Fed rate hike on Wednesday, as elevated energy prices continue to fuel inflationary pressures. Oil prices extended their gains on Monday after Saudi Arabia shut a key pipeline used to bypass the Strait of Hormuz following drone attacks. The latest rally in crude weighed on major US equity benchmarks last week, with the Dow losing 1.57%, while the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.8% and 0.66%, respectively.
